obligation: Payment facilitator notice of suspected card compromise
trigger: Suspected or confirmed unauthorized access to card data or to any account that can display or charge cards
deadline: Within 24 hours of suspicion (contract term; fictional)
notify: Payment facilitator risk line (owner calls, then confirms in writing in the facilitator portal)

obligation: Visa notification of a compromise event
citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised, version 10.0 (effective 2026-06-25), Section A.1
trigger: Evidence sufficient to raise a reasonable suspicion of, or to confirm, unauthorized access to Visa account data or a payment system
deadline: Within 3 calendar days of that discovery
notify: Visa, normally coordinated through the payment facilitator and its acquiring bank
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - card brand rule reaching the inn through the sub-merchant agreement; the facilitator coordinates

citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.2 and Attachment A
deadline: Within 3 calendar days of notifying Visa
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if Visa account data is involved

citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.4
trigger: Discovery of compromised account data, a Visa request, or a determined window of exposure
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if card numbers were exposed (email forms, displayed virtual cards)

obligation: PCI Forensic Investigator (if Visa requires one)
citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.5
trigger: Formal notice from Visa requiring a PFI investigation
deadline: Contract a PFI within 5 business days; preliminary report within 5 business days of contracting; final report within 10 business days of completing the investigation
applies_at_this_tier: Only if Visa requires it (Visa may instead require an independent investigation, Section A.6)

obligation: Other card brands: American Express verified; Mastercard and Discover not verified (contractual)
citation: American Express Data Security Operating Policy (DSOP), United States, April 2026, Section 3. Mastercard and Discover rules, applied through the facilitator, not verified: Mastercard's site returned HTTP 403 and no Discover rules page was found. Not law
trigger: Suspected or confirmed compromise of American Express, Mastercard or Discover card data (for American Express, a potential or confirmed compromise is a Data Incident)
deadline: American Express: immediately, and no later than 72 hours after discovery; then investigate, and engage a PCI Forensic Investigator within 5 days of discovery if 10,000 or more card numbers are involved (DSOP Section 3). Mastercard and Discover: per the facilitator's instructions (not verified); treat 24 hours as the working target
notify: American Express Enterprise Incident Response Program (EIRP@aexp.com, 1-888-732-3750), with a named company contact; Mastercard and Discover through the facilitator

trigger: Breach of security of electronic personal information of Florida residents. Includes a name with a driver license, ID card, or passport number (ID photos), and a name with a card number in combination with any required security code (emailed card forms)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (unless delayed under 501.171(4)(b) or waived under 501.171(4)(c))
notify: Each affected Florida resident, by mail or email

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day good-cause extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to notice to individuals)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs, with synopsis, count, services offered, a copy of the individual notice, and a contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500+ Florida residents (about 1,900 ID photos and 3,400 guest profiles exist; about 55% of guests live in Florida)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000 are notified

trigger: Owner decides, after investigation and consultation with law enforcement, that the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept at least 5 years; copy to the Department within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Only if this path is used; counsel decides

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines in writing that notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period the agency specifies in writing
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request

obligation: Third-party agent notice to the inn (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains, stores, or processes personal information for the inn (innkeeping software vendor, AI add-on, email provider) has a breach
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, and no later than 10 days after the vendor's determination
notify: The inn (owner-innkeeper); the inn then gives the 501.171(3) and (4) notices

trigger: Affected guests who reside outside Florida (about 45% of guests)
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - check residency of affected guests

trigger: Unauthorized access to the OTA-2 partner portal or messages sent to OTA guests by an attacker
deadline: Per the OTA's terms; treat as same day
notify: OTA-2 partner support (and OTA-1 if its account was reached)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual; the OTA can warn and protect its guests

citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.3.3.4 (recommended)
trigger: Suspected card compromise or payment fraud against guests
notify: U.S. Secret Service field office; FBI (IC3 online report)

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor

applies_at_this_tier: Only if coverage exists - no standalone cyber policy; whether the business owner's policy has a data breach endorsement is unconfirmed

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed only: 72 hours; 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25, and the inn is far below the proposed SBA size test

citation: FAR 52.204-25 (Section 889); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Covered equipment found while performing a federal contract
deadline: Within 1 business day. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the inn holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
